about: Tembusu, an architecture studio in Singapore, shows Teduh House before it is built: entry court → living room → pool deck, soft hazy tropical daylight, three different viewpoints with the camera moving the whole way.
made_with: The demo's pictures were made with GPT Image 2.5 and its moves with MiniMax H3 Max Turbo, as this skill's tools make them (their pictures come from nano-banana-pro). The prompts carry over.

living.prompt:
Real architectural photograph of the double-height living room of a newly finished tropical modern house, on a DIAGONAL view across the room, not square to any wall. The camera stands just inside the room near one back corner, 1.5 metres above the floor, and looks about 40 degrees off the room's long axis, so two walls recede in strong two-point perspective and meet at a tall vertical corner left of the picture's centre.
On the left, one wall recedes to that corner: full height, pale honed limestone in large panels laid in long horizontal courses, double height, about 6 metres tall.
On the right of the corner, the other wall recedes toward the camera and runs out of the right side of the picture: first a tall narrow fixed screen of vertical teak louvres, then a very wide opening 7 metres wide and 3 metres high whose full-height glass sliding doors in slim bronze frames are slid completely open and stacked at the end next to the teak screen, so the room is entirely open to the outside. Through the opening: a teak deck at floor level, then a long swimming pool lined in green stone tiles, then a lush tropical garden of palms, ferns and broadleaf planting, a stop brighter than the room but not blown out. Above the opening a calm band of fair-faced board-formed concrete rises to a teak-boarded ceiling.
Floor: cream terrazzo with small grey-green chips, honed to a soft, quiet sheen, filling the lower third of the picture. Furniture, in the middle ground, sitting on a clear area of floor: two woven rattan lounge chairs with teak frames and natural linen cushions, angled toward each other around a low round limestone table. Nothing else: sparse, calm, no rugs, no art, no lamps.
Light: soft, hazy, overcast-bright tropical daylight in the early afternoon, entirely diffuse. Low contrast. No direct sun anywhere in the room, no sun patches on the floor, no leaf shadows, no dappled light, no hard shadows, only very faint soft contact shadows under the furniture. Gentle glow on the floor from the open side. Natural, slightly muted colour, no HDR look.
Full-frame camera, 24 mm tilt-shift lens, perfectly straight vertical lines, clean, crisp, noise-free material detail. A real photograph, like a page from an architecture magazine. No people, no text, no signage, no logos, no art on the walls.
living.note: the master: the stop people care about most, made first

entry-first.prompt:
The same house as in the reference photograph, a new camera position, outside the house: the entry court on the opposite side of the living room from the pool. A real architectural photograph, in the same light, with the same materials.
The camera stands outside in the entry court, under the deep overhang of the roof, 1.5 metres above the ground, about 6 metres from the entrance, and looks STRAIGHT at the front wall, square-on, in one-point perspective, centred on the door. The front wall fills the whole picture from edge to edge: fair-faced board-formed concrete, the same concrete as the band above the opening in the reference, calm, plain and even.
In the middle of that wall, one tall doorway about 2.8 metres wide and 4 metres high, taking up about the middle third of the picture's width. Its top edge crosses the picture at about 40 percent of the picture's height from the top. Its tall solid teak pivot door stands wide open, turned 90 degrees, seen almost edge-on inside the right side of the doorway, so the doorway is clear. Above the doorway the concrete wall rises unbroken to the top of the picture: a plain calm area with nothing on it, filling the whole top 40 percent of the picture across its full width. Only a thin strip of the same teak ceiling boards shows along the very top edge.
Looking in through the open doorway we see straight through the same double-height living room to its far side: the same honed terrazzo floor running away from the threshold, the pale limestone wall receding along the left inside the room, the same two rattan lounge chairs and low round limestone table small and left of centre in the room, then the same wide opening with its doors stacked away and teak screens, the same timber deck, the same long green-stone pool crossing the view, and the same tropical garden beyond, bright and soft.
Ground of the entry court: large pale honed limestone pavers with fine joints, filling the bottom fifth of the picture, leading to the threshold.
Near foreground at the right side, close to the camera: a mature frangipani tree in a low board-formed concrete planter. Its trunk rises at about 85 percent of the picture's width, out of focus only very slightly, and its branches with long leaves and clusters of white-and-yellow flowers spread to the left across the right part of the wall. The highest leaves stop at about 30 percent of the picture's height from the top, so the top 28 percent of the wall stays clear of leaves everywhere; the lowest branch tips reach to about 65 percent of the picture's width.
Light: the same soft, hazy, bright tropical daylight, entirely diffuse, low contrast. No direct sun, no sun patches, no leaf shadows on the wall or ground, no dappled light, no hard shadows, only very faint soft contact shadows. Natural, slightly muted colour, no HDR look.
Full-frame camera, 24 mm tilt-shift lens, perfectly straight vertical lines, clean, crisp, noise-free material detail. A real photograph. No people, no text, no house number, no signage, no logos, no lamps on the wall.

entry.prompt:
This photograph has flat grey blank margins along its top, left and right edges. Paint those margins so the photograph continues seamlessly: keep everything already in the photograph exactly as it is, same position, same size, same light, same grain.
Top and sides: the same fair-faced board-formed concrete wall simply continues, plain and calm, with the same horizontal board marks, up to the top of the picture and out to both sides. A thin strip of the same teak ceiling boards runs along the very top edge, as in the original, moved to the new top edge; remove the old teak strip where it now crosses the wall so that the wall is one unbroken surface with nothing on it.
Right side: the frangipani tree's branches, leaves and flowers and its concrete planter continue naturally out of the right edge. No leaves or branches higher than they already are: above the tree the wall stays plain and empty.
Left side: only the wall and the pale limestone paving continue.
Same soft, hazy, diffuse daylight, no direct sun, no leaf shadows on the wall. A real architectural photograph, perfectly straight verticals. No people, no text, no signage, no logos, no lamps.
entry.note: a second edit lowered the door so the title has a calm wall above it

living-in.note: a crop, not a repaint: the room corner at the far left popped up beside the armchair during the turn. A repaint of the wall bent the floor line

deck-first.prompt:
The same house as in the reference photograph, a new camera position, outside on the deck: we have walked out through the wide opening onto the timber deck and turned to look ALONG the length of the swimming pool. A real architectural photograph, in the same light, with the same materials.
The camera stands on the teak deck, 1.5 metres above it, right beside the near end of the long pool, and looks straight down the pool's length in strong one-point perspective, its vanishing point a little right of the picture's centre. The water, a long ribbon of calm pale green over square green Sukabumi stone tiles with the tiles visible through the water, fills the centre and lower right of the picture and runs away from the camera for sixteen metres, its stone coping edges converging. No part of the living room interior is visible.
On the left: the teak deck boards running along the pool toward the far end, and above them the house itself, receding in steep perspective along the left side of the picture: a row of tall vertical teak louvre screens, the same teak as the screen in the reference, with the deep overhang of the teak-boarded roof above them, running from the left edge of the picture toward the far end.
On the right, across the water: the same lush tropical garden, palms, ferns and big broadleaf planting, growing right up to a low stone coping along the pool, its leaves softly reflected in the water.
At the far end of the pool: a plain low wall of the same pale limestone with planting and one big tree behind it, under the same pale hazy sky.
Light: the same soft, hazy, bright tropical daylight, entirely diffuse, low contrast, the sky a pale even white-grey. No direct sun, no sun patches, no leaf shadows on the deck, no dappled light, no hard shadows, only faint soft shadow under the roof. Natural, slightly muted colour, no HDR look.
Full-frame camera, 24 mm tilt-shift lens, perfectly straight vertical lines, clean, crisp, noise-free detail. A real photograph, like a page from an architecture magazine. No people, no furniture on the deck, no text, no signage, no logos.

deck-open.prompt: Edit this photograph. Change only the nearest part of the house at the far left of the picture (roughly the first fifth of the frame width, where the first big teak screen panel is). That part becomes the end of the wide living-room opening the camera has just walked out of: tall glass sliding door panels stacked fully open, side by side, in slim dark bronze frames, seen almost edge-on, with a glimpse past them of the pale limestone wall and the polished terrazzo floor inside, all under the same timber soffit. The vertical teak screens begin just beyond it and continue along the facade exactly as now. Keep everything else exactly as it is: the deck boards, the stone coping, the green-stone pool and its reflections, the garden, the palms, the sky and the soft hazy light. Same camera, same framing, same size. No people, no text.
deck-open.note: the screens nearest the camera showed closed where the camera had just walked out, so the video slid them shut: the end of the open living room had to show

deck.prompt: Edit this photograph: the same place, photographed again from about one and a half metres further to the right, away from the house, standing near the middle of the timber deck, at the same eye height, looking in the same direction straight along the pool, with the same lens. Because the camera is now further from the house, the facade on the left sits further back and looks narrower: the open end of the living room with its tall glass doors stacked open, then the vertical teak screens and the timber soffit, all a little further away and smaller in the frame, with a wider strip of deck boards in front of them. The pool, its stone coping, the garden, the palms and the far wall stay where they are in the view, only seen from the new spot. Same soft hazy light, same materials, same time of day. Photographic, sharp, natural perspective, verticals straight. No people, no text.
deck.note: the house too close on the left made the wall and doors push out at the end of the turn; the camera moved out onto the deck

move-1.prompt: One continuous, smooth, steady gimbal shot at walking pace, at a constant eye height of 1.5 metres. The camera starts outside in the entry court facing the concrete wall and walks straight forward through the tall open doorway, past the open teak pivot door, leaving the frangipani tree behind on the right. While it is still passing through the doorway it is already turning slowly to the left, and it keeps turning left as it steps into the double-height living room, about 40 degrees in all. It never looks to the right: the right-hand part of the room is never seen. It comes to rest looking diagonally across the room at the limestone wall, the teak screen and the wide opening to the pool, as in the last picture. Only the camera moves. The room holds only the two rattan armchairs and the round stone table: no sofa, no daybed, no other furniture. The walls stay plain and flat. The door stays still, the light stays soft and hazy, nothing else changes. No cuts, no people, no text.
move-1.note: four takes; every one invented a daybed on the right as the camera came through the door (no picture shows that side). The kept take let it appear from behind the door, stay on its rug and leave as the camera turned, like real furniture

move-2.prompt: One continuous, smooth, steady gimbal shot at an unhurried walking pace, at a constant eye height of 1.5 metres. The camera starts inside the living room looking diagonally across it, walks forward past the rattan chairs and out through the wide opening, past the glass doors that stay stacked fully open, onto the timber deck. It keeps walking out to the middle of the deck, a little away from the house, and only then turns slowly and gently to the left, coming to rest looking straight along the long green-stone pool, with the house's teak screens set back on the left and the garden on the right, as in the last picture. The house stays at a calm distance on the left the whole time; the turn is slow and even. Only the camera moves. The glass doors stay open, the teak screens never move, nothing slides, opens or closes. The chairs stay still, the water stays calm, the palms barely stir, the light stays soft and hazy. No cuts, no people, no text.
